title: Kissed with Chocolate French Beef Pot-au-Feu
description: A sweet and comforting French dish featuring tender beef, rich broth, and molten white chocolate chips. Perfect for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
instructions: Combine beef short ribs, vegetable broth, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a large pot-au-feu pot or Dutch oven. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 hours, or until the beef is tender.
Remove the beef from the pot and set it aside to cool. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
Add the white chocolate chips to the broth and stir until they are melted and the mixture is smooth.
Return the beef to the pot and stir to coat with the chocolate broth.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour to make a roux, cooking for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the red wine, bringing the mixture to a simmer and cooking until it has thickened slightly. Stir the roux into the chocolate broth and cook for 2 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened to your liking.
Season the sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the beef and chocolate broth hot, garnished with fresh thyme if desired.
Let the dish rest for 10 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
